Atoms to

One engine for every scale. Ask an AI to fill a scene with real, measured data, then fly through it at its true size — in a browser, on a phone or in VR. Nothing to install.

THE SCALE

36 orders
of magnitude.

Scenes already reach from a workbench to the edge of the observable universe: one unit is one light year, everything is at its real size, and a logarithmic depth buffer keeps a planet 10 km below you and a galaxy billions of light years away sharp at the same time. The next direction is inward — to molecules and atoms.

REAL DATA THROUGH MCP

Three steps
to a real sky.

The AI does the tedious part: it looks up the numbers in an astronomical catalogue, writes them into a simple scene description, and Spider Paint draws them. You get a link to open — and a list of anything that was left out, and why.

  1. Connect the public MCP

    In Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini, add a custom connector with no authentication:

    https://spider-paint.vercel.app/api/mcp

  2. Ask in plain words

    Name a region, a cluster or a planetary system, and ask for measured values. The agent writes a 3draft-sky catalogue in astronomers’ units — RA and Dec, parallax, spectral type, AU, Earth radii — with the source of every number.

  3. Open the link and fly

    The scene arrives as a link; the whole scene is packed into it and never touches a server. Use Enter to find an object, T to target it, 0 to orbit.

TRY ASKING

Make a scene of the Pleiades with its 50 brightest members from Gaia, and start inside the cluster. Show the 20 nearest white dwarfs and fly me to the closest. Build the Kepler-90 system with its eight planets and their orbits.

WHERE THE NUMBERS COME FROM

GaiaPositions, parallaxes, temperatures and radii for ~1.8 billion stars.NASA ExoplanetsEvery confirmed exoplanet: orbit, radius, temperature, host star.SIMBADOne object at a time: names, spectral types, distances.HYG120 000 bright and nearby stars — the source of the deep sky’s stars.

HONEST BY DESIGN

What is real.
What is drawn.

REAL

As measured

Positions, distances, sizes and colours, as precise as the catalogue. The Solar System’s planets where they stand on a given date.

MADE UP

Only when unknown

An exoplanet’s orbital plane, a galaxy’s tilt without catalogue axes, planet surfaces — plausible by class, never presented as observed.

ENLARGED

Where needed

Black holes are drawn bigger than real; a galaxy is a cloud of points, each standing for millions of stars.

IN THE CLASSROOM

Learn by
going there.

01

Feel the distance

There is no hyperspace jump. Fly from the Moon to Proxima Centauri and watch the speed levels climb.

02

Ask, then check

Students ask the AI for a star system, then compare the scene with the catalogue values it cited.

03

Build the model

From a lunar lander to a space station: model it in Spider Paint, alone or together with an agent.

04

Walk in VR

Open the same scene on a headset and explore it with bare hands.

NEXT: THE OTHER DIRECTION

Down to
atoms.

The same recipe — public data, an MCP tool, a scene at true scale — works below a millimetre too. The plan: load molecules and crystal structures from open databases, draw atoms by element and bonds as beams, and use the same targeting and orbit navigation that flies between stars.

This part is a plan, not a feature yet. Follow the journal for progress.
